original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-surjective-representable}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable
morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$. Then
$f$ is surjective (in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable})
if and only if $|f| : |X| \to |Y|$ is surjective.

statement:
Use the chapter’s definition of algebraic-space morphisms on the chosen big fppf site; a representable morphism has a property P only through all its scheme-base-change tests.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is surjective,
\item for every scheme $Z$ and any morphism $Z \to Y$ the morphism
$Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is surjective,
\item for every affine scheme $Z$ and any morphism
$Z \to Y$ the morphism $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is surjective,
\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is a surjective morphism,
\item there exists a scheme $U$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$\varphi : U \to X$ such that the composition $f \circ \varphi$
is surjective,
\item there exists a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
U \ar[d] \ar[r] & V \ar[d] \\
X \ar[r] & Y
}
$$
where $U$, $V$ are schemes and the vertical arrows are surjective \'etale
such that the top horizontal arrow is surjective, and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}

review_note: Independent comparison against pinned original theorem in prepared Stage A spaces-morphisms.tex:666; proofs not read; safe-viewer not executed. The source is the universal statement that surjectivity is closed under composition. Stage A mistakenly makes 'the composition of surjective morphisms' a hypothesis while restating the whole proposition as a conclusion. It must quantify over composable surjections as hypotheses and explicitly conclude their composite is surjective.
hold_reason: Incomplete quantified hypotheses and circular subject-as-hypothesis parsing.
proposed_correction: Let X→Y and Y→Z be composable surjective morphisms of algebraic spaces. Then X→Z is surjective.
